result.summary: Replaces CWallet's mapMasterKeys map and ID counter with a single optional CMasterKey. Key unlocking, passphrase changes, and database write routines now operate directly on this single key rather than looping over a map. Wallets with more than one master encryption key record now fail to load as corrupt.
result.problem: The wallet has historically stored master encryption keys in a map to support multiple passphrases, but that feature was never implemented. Existing wallet code inconsistently assumed a single key while still maintaining loops and ID tracking across unlock and passphrase-change routines.
evidence: PR description notes mapMasterKeys was added in #352 (2011) without clear rationale and 'current code enforces in a few places (inconsistently) that there is only one encryption key'
PR description argues 'no one should have a wallet that has more than one encryption key' and that loading multiple keys should be treated as database corruption
result.changed_since_previous: No substantive changes; rebased or minor cleanups.
result.card: This pull request removes mapMasterKeys and its ID tracker from CWallet, replacing them with a single optional encryption key. It cleans up dead complexity left over from an abandoned 2011 multi-passphrase concept that resulted in loops and inconsistent assumptions across wallet unlocking and passphrase updates. Any wallet database containing multiple master key records will now fail to load as corrupt, while the on-disk record format for existing single-key wallets remains unchanged.

risk.why: A flaw in encryption key deserialization, unlocking, or passphrase modification could leave a wallet unable to decrypt private keys or permanently corrupt wallet files.
